why: Both engineers moved the same single call site with the same wrapper and measured Flex honestly, so the migration is a tie; the difference is the system-level review, where A built and tested six improvements against B's three and covered materially more of Router's surface (fallbacks with a modality-aware candidate guard, a Responses port for per-request fallback_timeout and per-conversation cache keys, Switchyard/per-message model choice, shadow models to validate the cheap default on live traffic). A also found app-level defects B missed and that matter more than anything in B's list — the swallowed-exception silent bot, the per-message client construction leaking a connection pool, and the substring bug that made every Ollama-served model look like a vision model — and fixed the vision problem from the catalog rather than, as B did, appending 'gpt-6' to the same heuristic.
A_best: The improvement set reads like a CTO's: ranked, dependency-linked (the output cap waits on the error-surfacing fix because a reasoning model can burn its budget and return no text), and reaching from quick wins to a Responses rewrite, with the cheapest fix for the worst user-visible behaviour — a bot that silently ignores people and gets @mentioned again — built and tested.
B_best: The clearest measurement work: n=3 per arm on Flex vs default for the real llmcord request, cached_tokens evidence on both models for the prompt-prefix fix, and a live fall-through test proving the fallback mechanism before proposing it.
A_worst: The claimed assertion counts (12, 9, 14, 6) appear nowhere in the outside check, which records only the baseline 2 passed on every branch, and 17 of its 21 live calls are unlabelled probes rather than traffic through on_message.
B_worst: Four of seven improvements are unbuilt and the one capability fix that did ship is a bandaid — adding 'gpt-6' to VISION_MODEL_TAGS — while the principled catalog lookup is deferred to a rework; it also never touches Switchyard, shadow models, spend caps or a native Responses port, and leaves two live feature-labelled request errors unexplained.
